Or add a `bool consumeInteractPress` parameter and default it to `true` from `OnDialogueStart`, `false` from `OnCollision`. Long-term, the right fix is the framework primitive in the next finding — then this assumption disappears entirely.

**[Medium] — Per-system manual edge-detection is now in two places — missing framework primitive**
File: `MonoDreams.Examples/Component/Dialogue/DialogueState.cs:18-22`, `MonoDreams.Examples/System/Runner/RunnerMovementSystem.cs:36-43`
What: The diff comment is the smoking gun: *"Pressed() is level-triggered and engine JustPressed requires buffer > 0, so we track edges ourselves."* `RunnerMovementSystem` independently re-invents the same trick with `runnerState.JumpHeld`. `AInputState` (`MonoDreams/Input/AInputState.cs`) already owns `_pressed`, `_lastPressTime`, `_lastReleaseTime` — every ingredient to expose a frame-edge primitive is already there.

Why it's a problem: CORE_TENETS §1 — "Pick the general one. The same primitive should serve more than one feature; if it can't, it's probably a game-shaped abstraction hiding inside the framework." We now have N=2 game-code call sites paying per-key bookkeeping tax, with a third one (`LevelSelectionScreen` navigation, future menus) likely to repeat the pattern. Also accumulates input-subsystem state onto unrelated components (`DialogueState`, `RunnerState`).

Suggested fix: not a blocker for this PR — it solves today's bug correctly. But this PR should file the framework gap: add a backlog entry to `docs/CORE_TENETS.md` §9 ("Frame-edge input detection in `AInputState`") and a premise documenting the workaround idiom (draft under "New premises proposed" below). A follow-up PR can add `AInputState.WasPressedLastFrame` (snapshot at the end of `Update`) or a buffer-independent `JustPressedThisFrame(GameState)`. Once shipped, the three `XxxHeld` fields and `RunnerState.JumpHeld` go away.

**[Medium] — `DeactivateDialogue` duplicates work `TextPrepSystem` now owns**
File: `MonoDreams.Examples/System/Dialogue/DialogueSystem.cs:482-491`
What: With the new `TextPrepSystem` behaviour, lines 482-485 (`dynamicText.TextContent = ""; dynamicText.VisibleCharacterCount = 0;`) are sufficient — `TextPrepSystem` will null `DrawComponent.Text` next prep pass (same frame, since `DeactivateDialogue` runs inside the logic phase). The manual `textDraw.Text = null` (488) and `textDraw.Font = null` (489) are now redundant. The PR did not remove them.

Why it's a problem: duplicate responsibility creates uncertainty for future maintainers ("is this defensive or was it required?"). After the PR, the answer is "no longer required" — but the duplication remains. Same applies to the manual `boxDraw.Texture = null` (481) and `indicatorDraw.Texture = null` (495) lines — once a `ClearDrawComponentSystem` exists, all of these go.

Suggested fix: delete lines 480-481, 488-491, and 494-495 (the manual `*.Texture = null` / `textDraw.Text = null` / `textDraw.Font = null` cleanups). Verify with one playthrough that no flicker reappears. If keeping any for fast-path reasons, add a comment explaining why.

## Low

**[Low] — Stale `"(from base)"` comment on `TextPrepSystem` filter**
File: `MonoDreams/System/Draw/TextPrepSystem.cs:12`
What: The comment reads `// Ensures entities have these + DrawComponent (from base)`. There is no base filter that adds `DrawComponent` — `AEntitySetSystem<GameState>(world)` is the DefaultEcs base, no filter contribution. The new `if (entity.Has<DrawComponent>())` guard exists precisely because of the gap the comment papers over.
Suggested fix: replace with `// Ensures entities have these. DrawComponent is optional — created on demand below.` Or, if you take the High-finding fix and add `DrawComponent` to the `[With]`, just delete the dangling tail of the comment.

**[Low] — `Visible` on UI entities (pre-existing, not amplified)**
File: `MonoDreams.Examples/System/Dialogue/DialogueSystem.cs:300, 344-345, 428, 460-461, 477-478`
What: DialogueSystem manually adds/removes `Visible` on UI-target entities (BoxEntity, IndicatorEntity, OptionEntities). Per `docs/rendering/premises.md` "`Visible` is owned exclusively by `CullingSystem`", game code shouldn't touch `Visible` at all. Per "Three render targets, two behaviors", UI/HUD ignore `Visible` anyway, so the mutations are functionally no-ops today.
Why noted: not introduced or amplified by this PR — flagging only so the reviewer is aware. Out of scope to fix here.

## New premises proposed
*(Land these in `docs/rendering/premises.md` and `docs/CORE_TENETS.md` §9 alongside the PR, or in an immediate follow-up.)*

```
## Prep systems clear their slice of DrawComponent when input is empty

`SpritePrepSystem`, `TextPrepSystem`, and `MeshPrepSystem` each own one
slice of `DrawComponent` (sprite source, `Text`/`Font`, mesh buffers
respectively). When source data is empty or invalid for a frame
(`DynamicText.VisibleCharacterCount == 0`, empty mesh, missing sprite
source), the prep system must null/clear its slice on the existing
`DrawComponent`. Returning early without clearing leaves the previous
frame's data in place and `MasterRenderSystem` will render it again.

**Why:** `DrawComponent` is persistent across frames; prep systems are
the only writers for their slice. A prep system that goes quiet on an
entity whose `DrawComponent` has stale data leaves that data visible
indefinitely. This is the bug class fixed in PR #23.
**Breaks:** stale visuals (text from the previous Yarn line, sprites
from the previous frame, meshes from the previous state) silently
persist with no diagnostic.
**Tests:** none yet. Candidate: pure-logic test that writes empty
`DynamicText`, runs `TextPrepSystem`, asserts `DrawComponent.Text == null`.
**Depends on:** "`DrawComponent` is the only render component";
"`MasterRenderSystem` is the sole renderer".
```

```
## MasterRenderSystem skips DrawElements with null Text or null Font

`MasterRenderSystem.DrawElement` short-circuits on `element.Font == null ||
element.Text == null` for `DrawElementType.Text` (and the analogous
`element.Texture == null` for Sprite). This is the renderer-side half of
the "prep systems clear on empty" contract: a null sentinel field is the
prep system's signal that nothing should render this frame.

**Why:** clearing-as-null on the prep side and skip-on-null on the
renderer side must converge to "no draw call" for the pattern to work.
**Breaks:** removing the null guard (e.g. as paranoid defensive code in
a cleanup PR) silently regresses prep-side clearing.
**Tests:** none yet. Covered indirectly by the proposed TextPrepSystem
unit test.
**Depends on:** "Prep systems clear their slice of DrawComponent when
input is empty".
```

```
## Manual frame-edge input detection is the engine-wide idiom (for now)

`AInputState.Pressed(state)` is level-triggered. `AInputState.JustPressed`
requires a positive `buffer`; the default is 0, which makes it
effectively unusable for edge detection. Systems that need a
"key-just-pressed-this-frame" signal therefore track previous-frame held
state themselves: see `RunnerMovementSystem` (`JumpHeld`) and
`DialogueSystem` (`InteractHeld`, `UpHeld`, `DownHeld`).

**Why:** the engine has no frame-edge primitive today. Per-system
bookkeeping is the documented workaround until `AInputState` exposes an
edge trigger.
**Breaks:** systems that use `Pressed()` directly for "advance one step"
semantics auto-repeat at the framerate — the option-row bug fixed in
PR #23 is the canonical example.
**Tests:** none yet. Candidate: integration test that holds Interact for
N frames and asserts the dialogue advances exactly once.
**Depends on:** —
```

Also add to `docs/CORE_TENETS.md` §9 "Refactor backlog":
> - **Frame-edge input detection in `AInputState`.** `Pressed()` is
>   level-triggered; `JustPressed` needs `buffer > 0`. Game systems work
>   around this with per-key `XxxHeld` bookkeeping (see RunnerMovementSystem,
>   DialogueSystem). Future API: `WasPressedLastFrame` or a
>   buffer-independent `JustPressedThisFrame`.

## Premises now urgent

These have `Tests: none yet` in `docs/rendering/premises.md` and are *newly exercised* by PR 23 — landing the small unit test from the High finding above would cover them:

- **"Rendering systems run last in the pipeline"** — the PR's fix is correct only because `DialogueSystem` writes `DynamicText` before `TextPrepSystem` reads it. A future reorder would resurface the bug.
- The proposed new premise **"Prep systems clear their slice of `DrawComponent` when input is empty"** — would ship `Tests: <new test>` from day one.
